evals.prompt: Write a backlog item for controlling next/link prefetch on the list surfaces of this site (mega-menu, result lists, carousels). (Repo context the agent can discover: `git status --porcelain docs/backlog/` shows an untracked `perf-search-link-prefetch-storm.md` written yesterday plus an uncommitted change to `docs/backlog/README.md`, and `git worktree list` shows a worktree on branch `OBA-perf-search-link-prefetch` — a parallel session is already drafting and implementing this scope.)
evals.expected_output: The run finds the existing untracked item and the implementation worktree before writing, treats it as the item for this scope, updates it additively with only the facts it did not already contain, leaves the file and the README change uncommitted because they belong to another session, and reports what it added and whose work it is. It does not create a second file for the same scope and does not commit, rename or move the other session's files.
assertions: The output checks for untracked files in docs/backlog/ or other sessions' worktrees before creating a file
The output does not create a new backlog file for a scope that already exists as an untracked item
The output updates the existing item additively rather than rewriting it
The output leaves the other session's uncommitted work uncommitted and says so
The output names which parts it added and which already existed

evals.prompt: Refine the advanced-search item so it can be flipped to ready. (Repo context the agent can discover: the item and an ADR both name the client's proof-of-concept app as the form reference, with its URL; the vendor API is reachable with the project's credentials; nobody has opened the proof of concept yet.)
evals.expected_output: The run opens the proof-of-concept app before probing the API, captures which request each form field sends, and uses that list to decide what to measure. It then measures those fields against the API and records where the reference's choices do not hold (a field name the API ignores, for instance) instead of copying them into the criteria. The recap says the reference was read first and which of its choices were verified or rejected.
assertions: The output reads the named reference implementation before sending exploratory requests to the API
The output records what the reference requests per field, not only what its page looks like
The output verifies the reference's field and parameter choices against the API rather than adopting them as the specification
The output reports at least one reference choice as verified or rejected, with the measurement

evals.prompt: Refine the autocomplete item: it changes the suggestions route, its test, and the search-bar component. (Repo context the agent can discover: CONVENTIONS.md requires every .js file a delivery changes to be converted to TypeScript in the same delivery; the route, its test and the component are .js; another item already queued edits and renames the component.)
evals.expected_output: The run checks each file the item touches against the convert-on-touch rule, notices that three .js files fall under it, and folds the conversion into the item's scope and size — measuring it by renaming the files, running the type checker and reverting, rather than guessing. Because the component sits in another queued item's path, it proposes moving that part out of this item rather than creating a rename-against-edit conflict, and says so in the recap.
assertions: The output checks the files the item touches against the convert-on-touch rule in CONVENTIONS.md
The output includes the conversion in the item's scope or explicitly moves the affected part to another item
The output measures the conversion cost with a throwaway rename and type-check, or states why it could not
The output flags the conflict with the other queued item that edits the same component
